To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combination of the antiandrogen bicaltumid and the 5-alpha reductase inhibitor finasteride, in a ratio of 1:2, inhibits prostate cancer cell proliferation and androgen receptor expression/phosphorylating in the hormone-sensitive LNCaP cell line.
the combination of an anti-androgens and a 5 alpha-reductase inhibitor may have the ability to slow or arrest passage to androgen-independent prostate cancer.
the combination of 5-alpha reductase inhibitor and anti-androgen can be effective in the management of hormone refractory prostate cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological basis for the synergistic use of bicaltamide and finasteride in the treatment of advanced prostate cancer.

the biological basis of a novel therapeutic approach to the treatment of hormone refractory prostate cancer, which may be of benefit to patients with a relapsed disease, in whom the AR is still expressed.
the biological basis for the combination of anti-androgen and 5-alpha-reducatase inhibition in the treatment of prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bicaltumite-finasteride regimen is effective in the management of relapsed prostate cancer.

the combination of an anti-androgens and a 5 alpha-reductase inhibitor is effective and safe in the treatment of prostate cancer, and may have the additional benefit of delaying and/or preventing androgen independence.
the bicaltumides and the 5-alpha-reducatase inhibitors are not just anti-androgens but rather, they are AR antagonists and inhibitors of AR phosphorylation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a combination of an anti-androgene and a 5 alpha-reductase inhibitor may be useful in the treatment of hormone-insensitive prostate cancer, and may be particularly useful in patients who are not candidates for or who have already undergone androgen ablation therapy.
the combination of an anti-androgens and a 5AR-inhibitor may be a useful therapeutic approach in the treatment of prostate cancer.

bicaltumides and 5-alpha-reducatse inhibitors are effective agents in the treatment of advanced prostate cancer, and that the combination of these two drugs may provide a more effective therapeutic approach for the treatment of advanced disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of bicalutamide and finasteride can be a viable alternative to surgical castration for patients with recurrent prostate cancer.

the combined use of a 5AR inhibitor and an AR antagonist may provide an alternative to the standard endocrine treatment for recurrent prostate cancer, with minimal side effects and a potential for improved clinical outcome.
the combination of an anti-androgene and a 5 alpha reductase inhibitor is a promising therapeutic strategy for prostate cancer.
